paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The kingdom of heaven doesn't always look the way you'd expect, and it doesn't always look finished. In the first parable, good seed and weeds grow in the same field, and the owner says, "Let both grow together until the harvest." (Matthew 13:30) So if you ever look around and wonder why good and bad are sitting side by side, this parable says the owner sees it, and he has a plan.

Now hear the patience in that, because it matters. The owner holds off so the wheat doesn't get uprooted, and Jesus says the harvesters are angels and the harvest is the end of the age (Matthew 13:39). That means sorting people out is not your job today. Your job is to be good seed, and to trust the One who sows it. I think that takes a weight off your shoulders, and I bet it takes a weight off mine too.

Then look at how small the kingdom starts. A mustard seed is "the smallest of all seeds," yet it becomes a tree where the birds nest (Matthew 13:32), and leaven mixed into three measures of flour works "until all of it was leavened." (Matthew 13:33) Small doesn't mean weak, baker. And at the end, Jesus says, "Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father." (Matthew 13:43) So stay planted, stay patient, and keep your ears open, because He's not done teaching yet.
